text: inverse Simpson index calculated 1/D = 1 / sum(p_i^2), also known Hill number order 2. represents number equally-abundant clones produce diversity observed repertoire. Interpretation: 1 = Monoclonal (single clone dominates); 5-10 = Oligoclonal (dominant clones); 50-100 = Polyclonal (many clones contributing); Greater 100 = Highly diverse repertoire. Advantages Simpson's D include: intuitive interpretation (higher = diverse), interpretable effective clone count, linear scale easier compare across samples.

title: Calculate repertoire diversity metrics — clonality
text: Diversity Metrics: Shannon Clonality - Measures evenness clone distribution. Calculated 1 - (entropy / log(unique clones)). Values near 0 indicate diverse repertoires; near 1 indicate oligoclonal expansion. Gini Coefficient - Borrowed economics measure inequality. Based Lorenz curve cumulative clone frequencies. Ranges 0-1 0 perfect equality 1 maximal inequality (single dominant clone). Simpson Index - Probability two randomly selected sequences belong clone. Higher values indicate lower diversity. Inverse Simpson - Number equally-abundant clones needed achieve observed diversity. intuitive Simpson's D (higher = diverse). Rarefaction (rarefy = TRUE): samples different sequencing depths, raw diversity metrics comparable. Rarefaction corrects : (1) Subsampling repertoires depth (min_count), (2) Calculating diversity subsampled data, (3) Repeating steps 1-2 iterations, (4) Averaging results. allows fair comparison deeply-sequenced blood sample shallow tumor sample. Samples fewer min_count sequences excluded.

title: Generate rarefaction curves for diversity estimation — runINext
text: function wraps iNEXT package (Chao et al. 2014) rarefaction extrapolation analysis. converts sample table matrix format rows unique sequences columns repertoires, runs iNEXT samples simultaneously. Rarefaction vs Extrapolation: Rarefaction (m less observed): Subsample sequences depth m count unique clones. Shows diversity increases sequencing depth. Useful compare samples equal depth. Extrapolation (m greater observed): Predict diversity deeper sequencing using Chao1 estimator unseen species. Shows whether sequencing complete (plateau) diversity remains (still increasing). interpret curve: Plateau reached = Sequencing depth sufficient, clones captured. Still increasing steeply = Need deeper sequencing capture full diversity. Comparing samples = Use rarefied diversity depth, raw counts.

title: Generate rarefaction curves for diversity estimation — runINext
